messages:
Sam (support): Hey team — escalated from customer ACMECorp: big spike of 429s during a nightly batch job. They claim it looked like quota exhaustion but also saw latency spikes and some 5xxs. Can we get a dashboard + alerting playbook to attribute 429s to route/model/customer and recommend mitigations?

Alex (eng-sre): First pass questions: do we have the API key (redacted ok), route(s), and a sample request_id? Was it embeddings or generation or both? Also is this hosted or dedicated customer?

Sam (support): API key ends with ...AB12 (redacted). Primary complaints on `/v1/embeddings` (model=embed-large), but also a smaller batch on `/v1/generate` (model=opt-13b-q4). Hosted. Sample log line from their payload: 

```
request_id=abc123 status=429 route=/v1/embeddings model=embed-large api_key=acct-...AB12 tokens=512 x-rate-limit-remaining=0 x-rate-limit-reset=1680000000
```

Priya (observability): I can add the panels. Key metrics to show: `redwood.requests.count` (labelled by status), `redwood.requests_tokens_total` (labels: route, model, api_key), and `redwood.rate_limit.events` (label: reason). Suggested PromQL snippets: 

- 429s per API key (5m):
```
sum by(api_key) (increase(redwood_requests_total{status="429"}[5m]))
```
- Tokens consumed per route/model (5m):
```
sum by(route, model) (increase(redwood_requests_tokens_total[5m]))
```
- 429 rate as pct of total (5m):
```
sum by(api_key) (increase(redwood_requests_total{status="429"}[5m])) /
sum by(api_key) (increase(redwood_requests_total[5m]))
```

Priya: Also add `redwood.requests_latency_bucket` heatmap to correlate latency with throttles. We should tag metrics with `rate_limit_reason` so we can split token_quota vs concurrency vs per-route caps.

Jasper (eng-platform): For burst detection we need short-window aggregations (1s / 30s). Example to find top bursty callers: 

```
topk(25, sum by(api_key, route) (increase(redwood_requests_tokens_total[1m])))
```

Jasper: Also surface `x-rate-limit-*` header values in logs (we already capture them) and expose a calculated `quota_remaining_pct` for customer rows. For Dedicated customers also check `dedicated.capacity.usage` vs their committed throughput.

Olivia (support-lead): Alerts should be meaningful and actionable. Proposed alert rules: 

- ALERT: API_KEY_HIGH_429_RATE — when an api_key sees 429_rate > 5% AND absolute 429_count > 50 over 5m -> severity P2, notify support + eng-sre.
- ALERT: MULTI_CUST_RATE_LIMIT_SPIKE — if >3 distinct api_keys have 429_count>20 in 10m -> P1 (possible system-level ratelimiting / incident).
- ALERT: TOKEN_BURN_RATE — api_key token consumption exceeds their billing quota by >20% in 1h -> notify billing + support.

Sam (support): Good. One operational question: how do we distinguish quota exhaustion (billing/quota) from short-term burst throttles? Customers get different messages.

Priya (observability): Two reliable signals: 1) header `x-rate-limit-reset` / `x-rate-limit-remaining` present in logs -> per-customer rate limit. 2) `redwood.rate_limit.events` label `reason=quota_exhausted` vs `reason=burst`. We need to ensure ingestion pipeline preserves that label from the rate limiter. Dashboard should include a pivot table: api_key / model / route with columns: total_requests, tokens, 429_count, reason_breakdown.

Alex (eng-sre): Support playbook snippet (we should save as KB article): 

1) Ask for API key + timeframe + example request_id.
2) Run query: 
```
-- 429s for key
sum by(status) (increase(redwood_requests_total{api_key="acct-...AB12", status="429"}[5m]))
```
3) Check token spend: 
```
sum by(route, model) (increase(redwood_requests_tokens_total{api_key="acct-...AB12"}[1h]))
```
4) Inspect request headers for `x-rate-limit-*` and `x-quota-*` and attach to ticket.
5) If bursty -> recommend client token-bucket limiter and suggest example throttle values. If real quota exhaustion -> escalate to billing to check limits/upgrade.

Alex (eng-sre): Example client guidance to include in KB: 
```
// pseudocode token-bucket limiter
function allowRequest() {
  tokens = min(capacity, tokens + refillRate * elapsed)
  if (tokens < cost) return false
  tokens -= cost
  return true
}
```

Sam (support): Customer supplied a repro script they used for load testing: 
```
for i in {1..1000}; do \
  curl -s -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer acct-...AB12" \
  -d '{"input":["sample text"]}' &
done
wait
```

Jasper (eng-platform): That's a pure burst test. Recommend we add a small note in docs: avoid spinning 1000 parallel curl processes, use paced batches (e.g., 50 concurrent, backoff on 429). I'll add a snippet to the KB.

Priya (observability): I'll create a dashboard folder `Support / RateLimit Attribution` and add panels: 
- Timeseries: 429_count per api_key (5m)
- Heatmap: api_key x model 429 density
- Table: per-route token burn (1h) with links to billing/customer console
- Burst topk panel (1m tokens)

Priya: linking initial Grafana draft: https://grafana.internal/d/abcd1234/throttle-attribution (internal) — contains queries + panel descriptions.

Olivia (support-lead): Assign owners: @Priya build dashboard; @Alex author alert rules + playbook; @Jasper add header capture and quota_remaining metric to logs ingestion. ETA EOD for initial set.

Sam (support): I'll reply to customer with interim guidance (throttle client, batch smaller) and ask for any more logs. Will paste their follow-up here.

ratebot: Incident created: RL-2026-03-15-01 assigned to eng-sre (Alex).

Alex (eng-sre): Picking up now — will post dashboard & alert links as I create them.

Priya (observability): Dashboard panels created and pinned. Added `reason=quota_exhausted` label extraction in the logs pipeline for this customer.

Sam (support): Thanks all — closing loop with customer now. Will reopen if they still see issues after changes. :thumbsup:
